target_customer: Employees and informal workers in Colombia with recurring income and a bank account who want small advances or short loans
problem: Workers in Colombia run short of cash before payday and often turn to costly informal lenders known as gota a gota, while banks serve them poorly.
business_model: Consumer lending with fixed service fees rather than interest, funded by equity and warehouse credit lines
product_category: Salary advance and small-ticket consumer lending app

founders.name: Freddy Fernandez
founders.background_notes: LatamFintech says over eight years at JPMorgan in New York; Bloomberg Linea says over 15 years of investment banking.

founders.name: Leonardo Devincenzi
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him Co-CEO and co-founder, serial entrepreneur focused on Latam.

competitors.name: Bancolombia
competitors.what: Bank offering payroll advance in its app, needs payroll held at the bank

competitors.name: Banco de Bogota
competitors.what: Bank payroll advance in its app

competitors.name: BBVA Colombia
competitors.what: Bank payroll advance in its app

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit scoring on bank data via open banking and a mobile lending app, plus managing loan funding, was standard fintech engineering with risk modeling as the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Lending products are copyable by banks, but repayment data on informal workers and funding relationships build up slowly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Banks offered payroll advances only to their own payroll clients; Bancolombia later became a partner (alliance announced 2023 per press) rather than a copier.

market_need_then: Liquidity needs among Colombian workers during and after the pandemic; the founders cited the Walmart earned-pay trend and the prevalence of gota a gota informal lending.

identity.visual_style: friendly, blue accents with a blue heart emoji in titles
identity.voice_and_tone: plain, accessible Spanish, tagline 'Credito para todos'

branding.brand_signature: Mujer con M de Monet women's credit program, per a quoted executive in press

brand_strength.rationale: Regular Colombian press coverage and a women's inclusion program give some recognition, but the name is shared with the painter and other fintechs.

pivots.from: Selling to employers who act as intermediaries for salary advances
pivots.to: Going directly to users without employer intermediaries
pivots.why: Employer intermediaries slowed access for users, per Bloomberg Linea and LatamFintech (2021)

outcome_analysis: Monet kept operating through 2025 and raised a 24 million dollar Series A in December 2025 that mixes 4 million dollars of equity with a credit line. It moved from employer-sold advances to a direct-to-user app, scaled loans to hundreds of thousands of users and won a Bancolombia partnership, and now plans Mexico entry. Public funding between YC in 2021 and 2025 is not documented in sources found.
notes: Series A of 24M is equity 4M led by Comfama Ventures plus a warehouse line (up to 20M per LatamList, structured financing up to 18M per a Cuatrecasas snippet); conflict noted. In 2021 the company said it planned a 2 to 5 million dollar seed round but no closed seed was confirmed. Andres Londono is described as a co-founder or partner by Bloomberg Linea and as CEO in a 2022 WorkWeek Q&A title, and Forbes counts four founders; the YC page lists only Devincenzi. Founding year sources range 2019 to 2021; Bloomberg Linea says early 2020. The LatamFintech article date is not shown; it reports Sept 2021 coverage. No layoffs, acquisition or shutdown found.
